newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam finance minister wary of borrowing abroad.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam finance minister wary of borrowing abroad.

text.p: Vietnam's new finance minister, Nguyen Sinh Hung, said on Monday he was not seeking foreign loans to fill trade and budget gaps at the moment.

"We understand that this (foreign borrowing) will be a channel for Vietnam to mobilise money, but we will do it only when we have adequate conditions," Hung told reporters during a break in National Assembly proceedings.
"We don't think this would be a good idea. It is not a good way to solve budget problems by borrowing more," he added.
Hung, who succeeded Ho Te as finance minister last week, declined to give any timing for Vietnam's debut international bond issue.
The World Bank has been advising Hanoi to hold back from tapping the international bond market until it has restructured the roughly $1.0 billion of debt it owes to foreign commercial creditors.
Vietnam clinched an agreement in principle with the so-called London Club of creditors in May to restructure its debt, but is still discussing solutions with individual lenders.
"We are doing it in rotation," Hung said. "We have agreed in principle, but for specific countries we have to conduct negotiations."
